citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The facility is not following the treatment instructions of the attending veterinarian (AV) for the control of external parasites
in a herd of fallow deer. On 8/26/26 the inspector observed more than 50% of the fallow deer herd with mottled fur loss
beginning at the shoulders and extending horizontally onto the thighs. The exposed skin has turned black in color posing
a concern for an ongoing irritation and the presence of chronic inflammation. All fallow deer were in good body condition
as well as alert and curious to the inspectors presence. There were two instances where the inspector noted two different
deer nibbling at their skin for less than half a minute. The facility has not noted any scratching within the fallow deer herd.
The facility representatives stated the deer's coat appears this way seasonally after they shed their winter coat in the
Spring. On June 24th and 25th of this year, the facility applied Cydectin utilizing a spray bottle containing this solution.
The product was sprayed along their backs as the animals gathered for feeding. The amount of Cydectin administered to
each deer was unknown to the representative and without consideration to the individual animal's weight. They have
noticed the deer's skin continue to worsen with the rise in temperature, but have not contacted their AV again to re-
evaluate treatment.
After the inspection, the inspector spoke with their AV who indicated that he verbally instructed the facility to administer
Cydectin pour on according to its label and based on the animals weight. The AV expressed concern about the potential
for improper dosing done by spraying these animals. The AV indicated he would contact the facility again to ensure
proper administration of Cydectin. The facility is not administering the treatment to the fallow deer as instructed by their
AV. Failure to administer this parasiticide according to its proper dosage and as instructed by the AV can result in
underdosing or overdosing the animal and can render the treatment ineffective.
In consultation with the AV, the licensee shall establish and maintain programs of adequate veterinary care that includes
the use of appropriate methods to prevent, control, diagnose, and treat diseases and injuries. The facility must ensure
they are following the AV's instructions for the control and prevention of external parasites in the fallow deer.
Correct by 9/9/26.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
